newsitem.title: GERMANY: German BASF sees acquisitions - report.
newsitem.headline: German BASF sees acquisitions - report.

text.p: German chemical giant BASF AG expects to expand its gases and pharmaceutical units but has ruled out Schering AG as a possible purchase, a German magazine said on Wednesday.

In a news release ahead of Friday's publication, Manager Magazin quoted BASF chief Juergen Strube in an interview as saying BASF wanted at least a 15 percent share of the German gases market and was interested in acquisitions in that area and pharmaceuticals.
But he ruled out drugs firm Schering AG as "not an adequate complement" to its business. Strube said BASF was looking to achieve a turnover of around three billion marks from pharmaceuticals in 1996.
Strube also voiced concern over continued over-capacity and price competition in the chemicals sector, saying that European companies would soon be hit by capacity spilling over from Korea.
He also said that aggressive pricing tactics from competitors in the Czech Republic, Poland, Slovakia, hungary and Slovenia would have an impact on the west European market.
